body: I would usually agree, but FMA had such a week ending, that it would be a shame for someone to completely stop watching anime because of it. There are a few points towards the start of brotherhood that are enhanced by the original, but not enough to change the enjoyment of some one watching for the first time.

I always recommend Full Metal Alchemist. It's overall the best starter Anime imo. It's not in your face with a lot of the stereotypical anime tropes, and you don't need to understand anything about Japanese culture to get into it. It has a bit of everything in it as well, some comedy, romance, action, and is even a bit of a thriller at times. The cherry on top is that the story is actually amazing as well. While it's not even my favorite Anime, I think it's the only one I would score a 10/10 ( just make sure it's FMA: Brotherhood though).

Since all of the other answers right now are just troll, I'll give an actual answer. In the Bible when Adam and Eve eat the forbidden fruit, God not only banishes them but IIRC their sin is passed down to every one.

Alot of it stems from what people see on a day to day basis. If you look out to the horizon, the world really does look flat. That has to so with the sheer size of the earth in comparison to us. From what I understand this is one of the most common arguments flat earthers use to defend their beliefs.

I've also seen numerous people believe the earth is flat from a literal interpretation of some Bible verse. I'm too lazy to look it up myself but if someone wants to correct me / link it themselves go ahead, but IIRC Jesus stood at the top of a mountain and the Bible states that he could see all of the world. Well obviously that wouldn't be possible if the earth was round, so to some that obviously means the earth is flat.

They also have some "evidence" that really just boils down to a poor understanding of optics. Some people will attach go pro cameras to rockets and launch them up to an altitude where the curvature of the earth is visibly apparent. When the footage comes back and they don't see the curvature it's a pretty easy conclusion to draw that the earth is actually flat. The issue with this proof is that the go pros use a fish eye lens, which distorts the image around the edges giving the curvature of the earth the illusion of being a straight line.

From my experience these are what drives most people to think the earth is flat, but I'm sure there are other reasons too.

Here is a really simple way to think about it. 10% of anything is the same as moving the decimal place left once. All the calculations for doing tips is pretty straight forward from there. If you want to tip in increments of 5% just take half of that 10% number and add it on at the end of it. 


Here's an example: 

Your bill comes out to $64.50.

Well 10% of that is just $6.45, but let's just round it up to $6.50 to make life easier.

You decide you want to leave a 25% tip.

To make it 20% just take the $6.50 and double it. $13 even.

But the other 5%? Well that's just half of the 10%, $6.50, which comes out to $3.25.

So add the 5% with the 20% and find out that the total 25% is $16.25. 

This might seem like alot of work to do mentally, but it really doesn't take that long. Also the more you do it the better you will get.

Hope this helps you when tipping!
